## What

Fixes for PR 483 (trail 405, change 281, ADR 0028 T7) on `feat/relevance-output`, built on base ffe01fa8. There are four local commits; none is pushed:

- a79e1e15 is the main fix.
- 03fccc11 strengthens the watch model.
- The third commit adds `declaration_origin`.
- The fourth is the review round.

**Root cause.** Relevance evidence is derived state read from other files, but it was not part of the dependency model. Facts were also keyed by spelling instead of binding.

**Item 1 and finding d: stale evidence.**
- The props-type and body evidence is now read inside `resolve_component_tracked`'s dependency recording.
- Call sites are counted again for every revision.
- Both are joined at one sink, `Resolved::answer`/`into_parts`, which the lazy answer also uses.
- `next()` now also reports kept components whose layers changed.

**Item 13: the watch model.** `crates/core/tests/relevance_watch_model.rs` `watch_equals_fresh` applies random edits and checks that the watch and lazy sessions equal a fresh `extract()` after each one. The edits are:
- adding or removing call sites
- changing the forward target's own props
- renaming an export
- editing the props type
- editing a story

The model also asserts that edits change a `used` list at least 3 times.

**Item 2.** An ambient member passed at the floor now goes to `used`, as the ADR says.

**Item 3: schema 8 follows ADR 0028.**
- Schema 8 is now `InheritedLayer::used`.
- Removed: the `relevance` map, `Relevance`/`AsToday` and `ComponentEntry::relevance_evidence`. These are gone from the wire, `index.d.ts`, `caliper schema`, the docs and the changeset.

**Item 6.** There is one sink, `relevance::apply`. `annotate` is gone from the three merge paths, and `Evidence<'a>` borrows.

**Item 4: one origin function.** `caliper_docgen_core::origin::declaration_origin -> Origin { React, SharedDom, Dependency, Project }` replaces the three predicates:
- `is_dom_file` now reads `is_ambient`.
- `is_react_declared` and `dependency_types::is_react` read `Origin::React`.

`relevance_model` generates `@types/react` and `@react-types/shared` sources.

**Findings a, b and c.**
- a: a file-level tag bound in an inner scope is `JsxTag::Scoped`.
- b: `Pick` keys are looked up from the declaring file.
- c: a forwarding target reaches its bases' non-ambient members.

**Item 9.** A JSX spread of the props object is recorded only; `Body::is_complete` decides. Review fix: a spread inside a nested component still hands the props on.

**Item 12.** The dead story-args, `CallSites::used`, `Body::defaulted` and `Named::prop` are deleted.

**Parse cache.** Moves to version 42.

## Evidence

**Checks run, with exit codes.**
- nextest on core, semantic and cli: 1583 tests, exit 0 after the trycmd schema case was regenerated.
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- `just test-checker-lane`: exit 0. The worktree's `target/release` is a symlink to my own target dir; CALIPER_BIN is ignored by the recipe.
- `just semver`: exit 0. It reports "breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor or major changeset", which is the existing `.changeset/relevance-output.md` (updated in this change).

**Watch model sensitivity.**
- With the fix, the model passes.
- Mutation 1 (watch keeps the previous revision's call sites): the model fails ("watch: C2 … after add a call site").
- Mutation 2 (gather the evidence outside the dependency recording): the model still passes. That mutation cannot change output today. Every file whose reads change `used` is also read by the resolution itself. Forwarding and picked keys only decide typed rows, and typed rows are not written yet.

**Watch refresh time on gate-large.** I copied the project and edited one component file 8 times (`ChakraCarouselPropsProvider.tsx`, release builds).
- Median: 6.2 ms on base, 7.1 ms on the fix.
- Max: 7.5 ms on base, 8.3 ms on the fix.
- Load average was 6 to 17.
- gate-large has no JSX consumer files, so I could not time a consumer edit there.

**Identity diff, against the a79e1e15 binary.** Canonical JSON, checker on by default, `stats` stripped, base `relevance` stripped, new `used` stripped. The result was identical on all five corpora:
- gate-large: 938 components
- chakra-only: 788
- shadcn-ui: 2106 (both binaries exit 2)
- mantine: 853
- react-spectrum: 1738

No layer gains `used` on any corpus. `used` is a subset of `members`, and DOM layers (`React.ComponentProps<"el">`) carry no `members` yet. The ADR's DOM-layer `members` is a prerequisite I did not do. I re-ran it on the final head, 4bd65325: identical on all five corpora again, and `just test-checker-lane` exit 0 again.

**Golden snapshots.** The only change is that `relevance` is removed.

## Not verified

- **Item 10 is partial.** `picked` still comes from `props_type.rs`'s syntax, now read in the declaring file, and not from the lane's answer. Doing it properly means carrying the resolver's `Pick` key set (`alias.rs:81`) out of `ResolveState` beside the entry. It has no output effect today, since `picked` only decides typed rows.
- **DOM-layer `members` are not filled.** So `used` stays empty on real corpora.

**Open code-review findings (medium), not fixed:**
- Layers that only the checker adds never get `used`.
- `lazy_delta` does not report components whose `used` changed through call sites (the eager path does).
- Non-ambient rows `decide` makes for collapsed members are not written. This is by design, since the listing must stay identical, but the old map was their only carrier.
- The first lazy answer counts the whole project's call sites.
- Each revision recounts call sites even when the edited file's JSX did not change.
- `declaration_origin` widens the old predicates: `/node_modules/react/` now counts as React for `is_dom_file` and `is_react_declared`, and `/@types/react/` outside node_modules for the dependency loader.

**Other gaps.**
- The finding-a test was not run against base.
- `/code-review` covered ffe01fa8..HEAD before the review-fix commit.

"""Usage: t7-identity.py base-binary head-binary dir... — the T7 identity check: the canonical output of both binaries,
`stats`, `schemaVersion` and every component's `relevance` set aside, must be byte-identical; prints the relevance
tally of the head output."""
import collections
import json
import subprocess
import sys


def run(binary, src):
    out = subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--quiet', '--no-cache'], capture_output=True, check=False)
    return json.loads(out.stdout)


def strip(doc):
    doc.pop('stats', None)
    doc.pop('schemaVersion', None)
    for entry in doc.get('components', {}).values():
        entry.pop('relevance', None)
    return json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'), sort_keys=True)


base, head, dirs = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3:]
failed = False
for src in dirs:
    a, b = run(base, src), run(head, src)
    tally = collections.Counter(v for e in b['components'].values() for v in e.get('relevance', {}).values())
    same = strip(a) == strip(b)
    failed |= not same
    print('IDENTICAL' if same else 'DIFFERENT', src, len(a['components']), dict(tally), 'schema', b.get('schemaVersion'))
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

"""Usage: t7-identity.py base-binary head-binary dir... — the T7 identity check: the canonical output of both binaries,
`stats`, `schemaVersion` and every component's `relevance` set aside, must be byte-identical; prints the relevance
tally of the head output."""
import collections
import json
import subprocess
import sys


def run(binary, src):
    out = subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--quiet', '--no-cache'], capture_output=True, check=False)
    return json.loads(out.stdout)


def strip(doc):
    doc.pop('stats', None)
    doc.pop('schemaVersion', None)
    for entry in doc.get('components', {}).values():
        entry.pop('relevance', None)
    return json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'), sort_keys=True)


base, head, dirs = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3:]
failed = False
for src in dirs:
    a, b = run(base, src), run(head, src)
    tally = collections.Counter(v for e in b['components'].values() for v in e.get('relevance', {}).values())
    same = strip(a) == strip(b)
    failed |= not same
    print('IDENTICAL' if same else 'DIFFERENT', src, len(a['components']), dict(tally), 'schema', b.get('schemaVersion'))
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

386	/// The checker's `props` for `entry` without those an inherited source collapsed into a layer holds, and the notable
387	/// ones to move to `notableInherited` once merged ([`move_notable`]).
388	///
389	/// The collapse decision has one owner, [`CollapseInheritedProps::collapses`](crate::types::options::CollapseInheritedProps::collapses),
390	/// asked with the members of a source that reach the component. The structural resolver decides the sources it reads,
391	/// which are its layers here; a source the structural answer did not read (no structural prop and no layer has it as
392	/// its source) is decided by `cx` ([`CollapseContext::collapses`]). [`Layering::kept`] makes the same decision from a
393	/// [`LayerFacts`] of `entry`, before the answer's types are converted.
394	///
395	/// 1. A prop a collapsed layer names (`InheritedLayer::members`) is left to it, unless the structural answer lists the
396	///    prop itself (the component declares it again), or it is one of the layer's notable members: that one is merged
397	///    as any prop is (the component's default, the checker's type and JSDoc) and then moved to `notableInherited`,
398	///    replacing the structural entry, as for a layer made here.
399	/// 2. A source only the checker read becomes a collapsed layer when the owner collapses it, asked with the members
400	///    that reach the component: the props of the answer whose `parent` is the source, after any `Omit` or `Pick`, each
401	///    name once (the structural resolver counts the same; no declared count is asked of the checker). A prop `picked`
402	///    names reaches by name, as the structural resolver lists whatever a `Pick` selects: it is neither counted nor held
403	///    by a layer, and stays listed. `picked` holds names, not (source, name): a member of another source that has the
404	///    name of a picked key is also left out of that source's count and layer, so the prop is listed (shown, never
405	///    hidden) and the layer holds one member fewer than the structural one; at the threshold that source can be listed
406	///    instead of collapsed. The checker answers one `parent` per name, so the pair would not tell the two apart either.
407	///    `members` are the others and `totalProps` their number, what the layer holds. Its
408	///    notable props move to `notableInherited`, as the structural resolver keeps a collapsed source's notable members.
409	///
410	/// Applying it again to the entry it changed gives the same props and layers: a layer made here is then a layer of the
411	/// entry, which the first rule follows.
412	pub(crate) fn layer_checker_props<'a>(
413	    entry: &mut ComponentEntry,
414	    props: Vec<&'a Arc<SemanticProp>>,
415	    picked: &[String],
416	    cx: CollapseContext,
417	) -> (Vec<&'a Arc<SemanticProp>>, Vec<(String, PropParent)>) {
418	    // The notable members of the layers the entry has (rule 1), then those of the layers made here (rule 2).
419	    let of_entry = layer_notable(entry);
420	    let (layers, made) = checker_sources(
421	        &*entry,
422	        props.iter().map(|prop| (prop.name.as_str(), prop.parent.as_ref(), prop.react_declared)),
423	        picked,
424	        cx,
425	    );
426	    entry.inheritance.extend(layers);
427	    let layered: rustc_hash::FxHashSet<&str> =
428	        entry.inheritance.iter().flat_map(|layer| layer.members.iter().map(String::as_str)).collect();
429	    let unconverted = unconverted_type();
430	    let kept: Vec<&'a Arc<SemanticProp>> = props
431	        .into_iter()
432	        .filter(|prop| {
433	            layered.is_empty()
434	                || keeps(
435	                    &prop.name,
436	                    prop.parent.as_ref(),
437	                    (&of_entry, &made),
438	                    entry.props.contains_key(&prop.name),
439	                    &layered,
440	                )
441	        })
442	        .collect();
443	    // A kept notable member of a layer the entry has is merged over its structural entry (of that same source), which
444	    // keeps a description or tags only the structural pass has; `move_notable` moves the merged prop back.
445	    for (name, source) in &of_entry {

449	            && let Some(structural) = entry.notable_inherited.remove(name)

462	    );
